outcome: Government entities consolidate compute, storage and hypervisor onto one platform, freeing them from a separate virtualisation licence.
overview: Government entities revisiting their virtualisation costs face a decision with a long tail: the licence line is visible, but the migration effort, the skills change and the applications that will not move are not. The Nutanix Cloud Platform with its own hypervisor removes a separate hypervisor licence and consolidates compute and storage, which is a real saving where the incumbent is genuinely retired. The number that decides the case is not the licence differential but the count of workloads that cannot migrate, and that only emerges from assessment.

benefits.text: Compute and storage consolidate onto one platform with one lifecycle
benefits.limits: Sized from measured capacity and performance rather than from host counts or invoice history; a design built on the latter is a quotation with an architecture attached

benefits.text: The included hypervisor removes a separate virtualisation licence line
benefits.limits: Licence savings are real only where the incumbent hypervisor is genuinely retired; running both leaves two contracts and costs more than either

benefits.text: Capacity is added in known node increments rather than designed each time
benefits.limits: Node increments simplify planning and coarsen it; a small capacity need still buys a whole node

residency: Entirely on entity-owned equipment inside the entity’s own data centres

notFor.situation: An estate whose applications are certified only on the incumbent hypervisor
notFor.why: Vendor certification governs support, and a migration that breaks it trades a licence cost for a support gap

notFor.situation: A small estate where the platform overhead exceeds the licence differential
notFor.why: The saving is proportional to scale and the platform is not

scope:
Model: Redington solutions engineering with an accredited Nutanix implementation partner · Duration: 12–16 weeks to a migrated first wave, hardware lead time excluded
Support model: Vendor hardware and software support with a replacement term matched to entity criticality; Redington coordinates the vendor case.
1) Assessment — inventory, measured capacity, vendor certification checks and the exception list
2) Design — sizing, migration waves, skills transition and the incumbent exit date
3) Build — nodes deployed, platform and management established
4) Migrate and hand over — waves migrated, incumbent retired, operations handed over
deliverables: Every workload is classified migratable or excepted, with the reason recorded
Migrated workloads meet the performance profile recorded in assessment
The entity’s own team completes a platform upgrade unaided during handover
effort: 12–16 weeks to a migrated first wave, hardware lead time excluded
